research.summary: Convention-fix sweep research: pydantic-settings env-var case behavior, path-scoped rules, tooling availability on this NAS path, and the mandated README structure.

findings.topic: pydantic-settings v2 env var name matching (case sensitivity, env_prefix)
findings.conclusion: By default env var names are matched case-insensitively: a field `brot_base_url` reads env var `BROT_BASE_URL`. `case_sensitive` defaults to False (only True opts into exact-case matching) and `env_prefix` defaults to '' (empty), so with both unset the env name is the field name, case-insensitively. The repo's SettingsConfigDict (app/config.py line 24) sets only env_file='.env', env_file_encoding='utf-8', extra='ignore' - no case_sensitive, no env_prefix - so default behavior applies. Dotenv (.env) keys preserve case but are still matched case-insensitively under the default; extra='ignore' means unmatched .env entries are dropped silently (no ValidationError). Renaming BROT_* fields to snake_case therefore keeps reading existing .env files with zero changes needed.

findings.topic: Mixed-case field name BROT_base_url already maps to BROT_BASE_URL
findings.conclusion: Under the same default case-insensitive matching, the current fields `BROT_base_url` / `BROT_api_key` / `BROT_model` (app/config.py lines 31-33) already resolve env vars BROT_BASE_URL / BROT_API_KEY / BROT_MODEL - exactly what .env.example ships (lines 3-5). On Windows, os.environ normalizes env names to upper-case, which makes this trivially consistent; on any OS the default matching is case-insensitive. The rename BROT_base_url -> brot_base_url is therefore behavior-preserving in both directions (old and new field spellings both read BROT_BASE_URL). Implementation touchpoints to rename in the same change: settings.BROT_api_key and settings.BROT_base_url references in validation_problems() (app/config.py lines 83, 94) and the BROT_* rows of the README env-var table (README.md lines 66-68).

findings.topic: Python path-scoped rules in global opencode config
findings.conclusion: C:\Users\Brent\.config\opencode\rules\ contains exactly three files: flutter.md (paths **/*.dart, **/pubspec.yaml), go.md (paths **/*.go, **/go.mod), rust.md (paths **/*.rs, **/Cargo.toml). There is NO python.md and no rule whose paths glob matches *.py. No path-scoped rule applies when touching .py files in this repo; implementation briefs rely on the global conventions (snake_case, no comments/docstrings, ~500-line modularity, job logs) and the global README corroborates this (rules/ line: 'go.md . rust.md . flutter.md').
